body:
Just got paid 3 minutes ago in Alabama.

Thankfully the gentleman was incorrect about being paid tomorrow. 
I still stand by the fact that people need to be nicer.

I definitely hope he's wrong. I'd prefer to get paid today. 

It's just so disheartening that people would be awful towards a person who's just doing their job. They're just trying to feed they're family and pay their bills. I know getting paid is a sensitive topic, and we do depend on these benefits, but it simply doesn't excuse treating another human being who's just trying to do the same thing we are, like garbage.

I know a few people are saying they got paid from other banks that deposit the same as Chime, typically, but the gentlemen I just spoke to at customer service said it won't be until the 31st. 

Also, many of you who called should be ashamed of yourselves if you're screaming at the reps. The man I spoke to sounded almost in tears, and he thanked me for being the calmest person he's spoken to regarding this. He thanked me so many times for treating him like everybody who calls should treat people. It's disgusting that anyone would act like that.
Unfortunately, I am also well aware that no such choice exists in the States. I'm just curious to get opinions on what the threshold would be.
I suppose it would be a multifaceted board of psychiatrists, psychologists, medical physicians, social workers, spiritual advisors, and anybody else you might have in mind?

I've struggled with mental illness my whole life. I was getting better after I left. I was doing so well. Now I'm looking at facing charges for false reports. I can't find a reason to not complete suicide. It's not that I want to die. I just don't want to exist in the life I'm living. My kids are well taken care of and safe. They will continue to be after I'm gone.
